chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding pure sable (fur), that there is no problem with it. But as for that in which the fur of rabbits is mixed, or other than that which resembles this, then do not pray in it.

key_terms.الْخَزِّ: Sable, a type of small marten known for its valuable fur
key_terms.فَلَا تُصَلِّ فِيهِ: So do not pray in it
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in clothes made of rabbit fur or mixed furs according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between pure sable (khazz) and mixed furs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ritual purity (taharah) in the garments of prayer. It highlights the scholarly nuance that while pure animal fur is permissible, mixtures or imitations that resemble prohibited materials render the prayer disliked (makruh), underscoring the importance of material authenticity in acts of worship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, raising it,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the pure otter (skin) that there is no problem with it, but as for that wherein is mixed the fur of rabbits or other than that from what resembles it, so you cannot pray Salāt in it’.
en.sarwar: 26. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who, in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about pure al-Khazz has said, ‘It is not an offense to perform Salah (prayer) with it,
but do not perform Salah (prayer) with that which is mixed with fur of foxes or other things.’”
